description: Feature inventory for the academic-writer plugin. A checklist for future audits: each top-level feature lists its subfeatures, the source of truth, runtime status, and known issues. status: ok | partial | broken | missing. Regenerate/extend this file whenever features are added or removed.

subfeatures.name: Init wizard (Preflight, Integrations, Profile incl. author_key, Gemini Onboarding, Style Analysis, Sources) with --quick mode
setup skill — standalone interview-driven onboarding wizard (Gemini key incl. live-tested GOOGLE_API_KEY, Python deps, optional CandleKeep/NotebookLM detection, sample-paragraph checkpoint)
subfeatures.issue: Reworked in commit 97594b9 (a3): setup is no longer a thin wrapper delegating to init --quick. It is user-invocable: true (src/skills/setup/SKILL.md:4) and a full independent 267-line, one-question-at-a-time wizard with its own preflight, Gemini key live-test via mcp__gemini-api__gemini_raw, and closing profile summary; init/SKILL.md:12 and setup/SKILL.md:13 cross-reference each other for the deeper vs quick path instead of one delegating to the other. Both remain safe to re-run and interoperate via the shared profile schema. Step 3 (Gemini API key) now offers plugin configuration (claude plugin install/config --config google_api_key=...) as the recommended, securely-stored option alongside the pre-existing env-var and secrets.json choices; init/SKILL.md Phase 3.5 mirrors the same three options for consistency.

features.name: Thesis + outline (article logical structure)

subfeatures.name: Mode B: structured outline + word/paragraph sizing
subfeatures.issue: Sections exceeding thresholds.json writerUnit.maxWords are now decomposed into a units[] array of writer-unit subsections sized within writerUnit.minWords-maxWords (target writerUnit.targetWords), adjacent tiny units merged; decomposition is prompt-enforced (markdown agent instructions), not code-enforced
subfeatures.notes: The units[] word-bound decomposition (thresholds.json writerUnit.minWords/maxWords/targetWords) is enforced only by prose instructions in src/agents/architect.md (lines ~91-101) — no script validates it and no such script exists under src/scripts/. src/skills/write/SKILL.md Step 5.5 ("Argument Graph Validation") checks orphan claims, depends_on cycles, and topological ordering, but never checks that a unit's word count actually falls in range or that adjacent tiny units were merged — verified by reading both files.

subfeatures.name: Explicit premise→support→thesis-link logical model
subfeatures.issue: Every section and writer unit now carries an argument-graph node (id, claim, evidence[], depends_on[], thesis_link, argument_role nested as a field); validated up front by write/SKILL.md Step 5.5 (orphan/cycle/empty-evidence/topological-order checks) before section-writers are spawned, not just post-hoc in self-review

subfeatures.name: Mode C: ownership-only from user draft

features.notes: Rolls up from the outline subfeature (see its own notes): the writer-unit word-bound decomposition it performs is not verified anywhere in the pipeline, so the parent stays partial until that subfeature does.

generate-docx.py creates Word output; author comments and runs /academic-writer:revise

features.name: Post-section synthesis + review

subfeatures.name: Cross-section and unit-to-unit coherence/flow review
subfeatures.issue: synthesizer.md now checks Argument Graph Fidelity — that delivered prose actually advances each unit/section's declared claim, that depends_on dependencies are built upon in the text (not just declared in the outline), and that the thesis_link chain genuinely reaches the thesis in the final prose; also checks subsection-to-subsection (unit-to-unit) transitions within a section, not only section-to-section

features.notes: No automated test (pytest or e2e) exercises src/agents/synthesizer.md or src/skills/review/SKILL.md's scorecard logic — grepped tests/ and tests/e2e/ for 'synth' and 'review', 0 behavioral hits; tests/test_plugin_structure.py only checks that synthesizer.md exists and is on the agent whitelist, not that its coherence/repetition/abstract checks do anything correct.

subfeatures.notes: The Hebrew no-year fix ("(מחבר, עמ' N)" vs "(Author Year, page)") landed only in plugins/academic-writer/mcp/gemini-server/src/tools/write_section.ts (verified by grep). gemini_edit and gemini_synthesize (src/tools/edit.ts, src/tools/synthesize.ts) contain no citation-style-aware prompt logic at all, so a synthesis or edit pass through Gemini does not enforce the same Hebrew no-year rule that write_section.ts now does.
